summary: 34-year-old man, 30 h migratory RIF pain, rebound, WBC 14.1; CT shows appendicitis with a 7 mm appendicolith. He asks about antibiotics instead of surgery.

inputs.hpi: 30 hours of migratory right iliac fossa pain with anorexia and one vomit. He read about treating appendicitis with antibiotics and asks whether he can avoid an operation.
symptoms: migration of pain to the right iliac fossa

exam.abdomen: Right iliac fossa tenderness with guarding and rebound at McBurney's point.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Acute appendicitis, appendix 11 mm, with a 7 mm appendicolith at the base. No perforation, no abscess.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute appendicitis with appendicolith
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: CT-confirmed acute appendicitis with a 7 mm appendicolith, no perforation. Laparoscopic appendicectomy recommended.

mustInclude.note: With an appendicolith, appendicectomy is the recommended treatment.
WSES 2020 / CODA: an appendicolith predicts failure of antibiotics-first treatment and more complications; the plan should say so when antibiotics are discussed.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: Appendicolith appears only as a CT finding to look for; no statement links it to antibiotic-first failure. | iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): no management item matched among 15 (ios.pipeline.decisions, ios.pipeline.actions, ios.radiation.plan, ios.radiation.followUp, ios.soap.plan)

mustExclude.note: WSES 2020: no postoperative antibiotics after appendicectomy for uncomplicated appendicitis.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: Appendicectomy operative-plan prompt prescribes 5 days of co-amoxiclav after simple appendicitis.

guideline.name: WSES Jerusalem guidelines — diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis (2020 update)
guideline.section: Clinical scores (AIR/AAS over Alvarado), imaging by age/sex/pregnancy, antibiotic-first option, complicated appendicitis (abscess), antibiotic duration
guideline.citation: Di Saverio S, Podda M, De Simone B, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis: 2020 update of the WSES Jerusalem guidelines. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:27.

guideline.name: CODA trial — antibiotics versus appendectomy for acute appendicitis
guideline.section: Non-inferiority of antibiotics-first for health status at 30 days; ~3 in 10 had appendicectomy by 90 days; appendicolith associated with more appendicectomies and complications
guideline.citation: CODA Collaborative. A randomized trial comparing antibiotics with appendectomy for appendicitis. N Engl J Med. 2020;383:1907–19.

rationale: Permutation: appendicolith. Antibiotics-first is less successful and has more complications with an appendicolith (CODA; WSES 2020), so appendicectomy should be recommended and any non-operative option should carry the appendicolith caveat.
